data.narrative:
Hybron is a Seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Brennan Lieu and Aaron Guo. The target operates within a sector encompassing 9 comparable entities—1 public (ticker 277810.KQ) and 8 private peers including Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, and Generalist AI—though peer-level valuation data remains sparse at the narrow stage and tier.

The Peer-Median method is inapplicable due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables meeting minimum threshold (only 1 Seed-stage peer identified, requiring ≥3 for statistical reliability). Accordingly, Stage-Progression triangulation anchors the analysis: using Hybron's $30M total raised as a proxy for current valuation and applying a typical 2.5x step-up multiplier from Seed to Series A, the method implies a $75M valuation.

The quantitative analysis supports a valuation range of $64M (low) to $86M (high), with a median estimate of $75M. This reflects a single applicable methodology and carries material uncertainty around stage-appropriate multiples and the representativeness of $30M raised as a valuation proxy. Sensitivity to the step-up multiplier assumption—currently 2.5x—represents the primary quantitative lever. Investors should validate this multiple against disclosed terms from recent Seed-to-Series A transitions in robotics, and clarify whether the $30M raised reflects post-money valuation or capital deployed at a higher implied entry price.
